Release asset not found during Stage B download
bugs.notes: Root cause: Load release metadata step in stage-b.yml did a single, no-retry read of /releases/tags/<tag>. GitHub release-asset reads are eventually consistent: when stage-a.yml dispatches Stage B via workflow_dispatch immediately after softprops/action-gh-release finishes uploading source_input.bin, the first read from a fresh runner can return the release without that asset yet visible, or with it in a transient state (starter/new) where a download would fail. This matches the reported intermittent nature (only fires when the specific runner+API-node the dispatch lands on has stale cache) and the fact that it worked previously (used to be luckier / smaller Stage A tail latency). Fix: bounded polling loop with backoff (0,3,3,4,5,5,10,15,20,25s -> ~90s total across up to 10 attempts) that only accepts an asset whose state is uploaded or absent (older responses omit the field). Logs visible assets on each attempt so a genuine miss is diagnosable. Also added a 3x retry with backoff on the asset-download call itself for unrelated transient 5xx/connection resets on large asset downloads. Confidence: high on the mechanism; not verified against a live GitHub-side retry (cannot repro the exact race in sandbox). If the asset never lands within 90s it still fails loudly with the same error, but now with per-attempt asset-list logging.

bugs.title: Clone-update-push settings not appearing for main account
bugs.notes: Root cause: the previous sweep never actually implemented this feature; the current codebase had no clone-update-push wiring at all in bot/src/index.js or bot/src/views.js. The Settings > GitHub clone sub-screen only offered Create/Connect/Disconnect, so the main account (which is itself a connected clone of motionssalt/clipforge) had nothing to click. Design decision: GitHub PATs cannot push to another user private repo, so a truly remote push from main account to other users clones is not possible. The correct shape is a per-clone pull-from-source action, which is what the legacy browser Settings page (_legacy/shadow-clone.js) exposed as Check for updates / Apply update. Fix: added bot/src/clone-sync.js with checkCloneUpdates (uses GitHub compare API against .clipforge-sync.json marker, or full snapshot if no marker) and applyCloneUpdates (single tree commit against current main HEAD with base_tree so per-clone paths branding/ jobs/ audio-library/ key/account files are preserved via the existing sourcePathAllowed excludes). Wired a Sync from source button into Settings > GitHub clone that shows only when a clone is connected (no is-main-account gate, no has-existing-clones gate). Flow: press Sync from source -> preview of changed files (first 20) with count and old->new SHA -> Apply update button -> commits into clone and updates .clipforge-sync.json. Confidence: high on wiring and design; button will render for every connected clone including main-account owner (satisfies the visibility complaint in bug-21). Not runtime-verified end-to-end against a live clone since that requires a real Cloudflare Worker deployment plus a real Telegram interaction, but node --check passes and I traced every call site. Preserved test failures (4 tests) are pre-existing due to missing tweetnacl npm install in sandbox and unrelated to this change.

bugs.title: On-demand video delivery for finished tasks
bugs.notes: Implemented on-demand video delivery for finished tasks. runtime.js taskKeyboard: every 'complete' task now gets a '📩 Send video to chat' button (task:sendvideo), works for single tasks and series Stage B parts since the button is keyed to state==complete regardless of publish status. index.js: new deliverVideoToChat handler — resolves the release tag from status.release_tag (fallback clipforge-<job_id>), locates the final.mp4 asset via new github.js findReleaseAsset() which honours the uploaded-state rule from bug-20. Size gate: if asset.size is 0/unknown or > 49 MB (1 MB headroom under the 50 MB Bot API limit) the bot replies with a direct browser_download_url link plus the release page link instead of attempting an upload. Under the limit it downloads the bytes with an authenticated octet-stream fetch (downloadReleaseAssetBytes, capped at 50 MB) and sends via new telegram.js sendVideoBytes (multipart sendVideo, supports_streaming). Caption is built from production.json (title + hashtags) via deliverVideoCaption, truncated to Telegram's 1024-char caption limit, with a 'ClipForge video — Task <label>' fallback when no plan title exists. A progress message is shown while the Worker downloads the asset. Confidence: wiring is verified (node --check passes, call sites traced); not runtime-verified against live Telegram/GitHub since that needs a deployed Worker and a real release asset. The ≥50 MB branch relies on GitHub's reported asset.size; a misreported size would surface as a Telegram send error, which the existing callback error path already reports to the user.
